Content: Students are studying relationships in ecosystems. Figure `1` shows a partial food web of an ecosystem.
problems/IL25G5S/media/1a.jpg
Which statement describes a relationship between producers and consumers?

A.Choice: Producers are a source of food for some consumers.

B.Choice: Consumers are a source of food for some producers.

C.Choice: Producers rely on only consumers to recycle nutrients back into the soil.

D.Choice: Consumers rely on only producers to recycle nutrients back into the soil.

Content: Fish have a special sensory organ system that includes a line on both sides of their body. The line detects the movement of other animals and objects in the water. Figure `1` shows the fish sensory organ system.
problems/IL25G5S/media/2a.jpg
Which statement describes the path of information in the fish when it responds to movement in the water?

A.Choice: The eyes send signals to the sensory hairs, which then send signals to the muscles.

B.Choice: The sensory hairs send signals to the brain, which then sends signals to the muscles.

C.Choice: The eyes send signals to the brain, which then sends signals to the sensory hairs, which then send signals to the muscles.

D.Choice: The sensory hairs send signals to the eyes, which then send signals to the brain, which then sends signals to the muscles.

Content: Students are studying cacti that live in different environments. Table `1` compares `text(two)` different species of cactus found in different areas of the United States.
problems/IL25G5S/media/3a.jpg
Which type of cactus is better adapted for areas that have cold winters, and why?

A.Choice: Type `1`, because many spines help protect the plant from sun damage

B.Choice: Type `1`, because growing close to the ground helps keep the plant warm

C.Choice: Type `2`, because branching arms help absorb more water

D.Choice: Type `2`, because water in the stem freezes when the temperatures drop

A city is investigating how to prepare for earthquakes. Which investigation will `bbtext(best)` determine the likelihood of an earthquake in the city?

A.Choice: Locate the nearest rivers and aquifers.

B.Choice: Locate the nearest ocean and coastline.

C.Choice: Locate the nearest natural sources of gas and oil.

D.Choice: Locate the nearest tectonic plate boundaries and faults.

Content: A wave buoy is a device used to convert energy. The device is made of a buoy and a generator that produces electricity. The buoy floats on deep ocean water, and the generator is attached to the buoy above and the seafloor below. Figure `1` shows a model of the device.
problems/IL25G5S/media/8a.jpg

:ibox:• Describe the type of energy that the wave buoy converts into electrical energy.

• Explain how larger waves will affect the electrical energy produced by the generator.

• Identify `bbtext(one)` type of energy that the wave buoy `bbtext(cannot)` convert into electrical energy given its current design.
A teacher heated `text(100 grams)` (`text(g)`) of `text(three)` different liquids in open beakers for `text(5 minutes)`. Table `1` shows the weights of `text(each liquid)` before and after heating.

Which statement best explains why the weight of `text(each liquid)` changed?

A.Choice: Heating caused some liquid to burn.

B.Choice: Heating caused some liquid to change into gas.

C.Choice: Heating caused some liquid particles to get smaller.

D.Choice: Heating caused some liquid particles to be destroyed.

Content: Students make a fruit-flavored drink. They add a drink powder to a glass of water. Figure `1` shows a model of the particles before and after the drink powder is added to the water.

Which statement `bbtext(best)` describes what happens to the drink powder when it is mixed into the water?

A.Choice: The particles of drink powder increase in size.

B.Choice: The particles of drink powder change into water particles.

C.Choice: The particles of drink powder spread throughout the water.

D.Choice: The particles of drink powder change phase from solid to gas.
